video_title: Darren Waller Went From Addiction and Rehab to NFL Stardom… Then Walked Away

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: athletes Darren Waller wants to collaborate with musically
quotes.quote: I mean Damian Lillard is definitely tough. Jello. Um, I don't know too many who else making music like that. Miles Bridges is the next one I can name. He's nice. I'll get it. Lu Will maybe? I'll get in the studio with him.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: players masking weakness and suffering in silence in pro sports
quotes.quote: I will say a lot. You got to be good at masking it. A lot of guys, you come in that environment, it's a hyper-competitive environment. It's like, you can't show signs of weakness. I don't want to show this here. This could be used against me. They could want to find somebody else that maybe has their more their shit together that they'll put in my space. So I got to hold this shit. I got to provide, I got to do whatever it is. Those are all legit reasons to show up and not show those signs of weakness. So I totally get it. But there's a lot of dudes suffering in silence. You see how many dudes, I remember Vincent Jackson, they found him dead in the room, dead at 40. Players dying 41, dudes offing themselves at 25.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: hiding his addiction from teammates during training camp
quotes.quote: I was really good at hiding it. There was one time Steve Smith Sr. was the vet in the receiver room. He was the best OG ever. We had a training camp. We would stay at the Hyatt Place hotel and I was in my Jeep rolling up in the parking lot. I hear 'do, do, do' on the window. I'm like, 'Oh shit!' And it was Steve just messing with me or whatever. But yeah, he was the OG for real, who I was looking to and modeled like, 'Oh, I'm seeing greatness every single day from this dude.' So I'm going to just do what he does.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: being suspended and facing public criticism while struggling with addiction
quotes.quote: That shit definitely stung for real. Seeing people, I was definitely more on the internet, searching my name, searching what people were saying back then. It's tough because I'm trying my best to hold things together in my life, but I'm struggling and I'm using these things to cope with what I'm dealing with. But most people's reaction, they see that, they see your name go across the ticker, they're like, 'This nigga bullshitting.' As opposed to being like, 'What's going on in his life?' Like having an understanding. But I get it. I got banned for a year in 2017. After that, I'm getting faced with real life. Football looks like it's just over with at this point.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: almost dying from a fentanyl-laced pill in Baltimore
quotes.quote: I was in Baltimore at the time and it was really easy to come across Percocet. I told you all in the beginning it was like the 5 milligrams. Now we're doing like 30 milligrams. These dudes we would buy from them, they were like, 'Be careful out here, they're pressing logos on pills. You could be thinking something, but it could be fentanyl.' I'm just like, 'That shit ain't never going to happen to me.' That day, I went pick some up. I always just snort one on the drive just to get the buzz going. Then take the rest when I got home. I pull up to this giant parking lot, which is like a grocery store out there, and I was going to get out of the car. But then I was like, 'I feel like I'm just going to crack like an egg on the ground if I fall out' because I felt like the pills were kicking in. I was like, 'I'm just going to sit in the car.' Turn the car off and then it was like somebody pulled the plug from behind the TV, like the power went out. It felt like I just laid my head back for a second and then woke up. It was like night time. I was sweating like I lost 15, 20 pounds. I'm in a hot car in the summer in August with the car off. That was enough for me to be like, 'Whoa.' That could have been my last. 'Fuck beating drug tests and all this shit, I'm willing to take a different route.'

quotes.speaker: Stephen Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Jackson's near-fatal pill overdose as a teenager
quotes.quote: I had my own experience as a teenager with pills. I almost killed myself. I ain't really talk about this. My mama tell you I almost crashed the car. I was turning off the main street after I dropped my friend home from being up two days on pills. We weren't going to school or nothing. And on the street I lived on, there wasn't no street lights. So I come off the main street with all the lights and I turn the street and it's just dark. So I just go, 'Oh, it's dark.' I just go to sleep behind the wheel. Hit the curb. I'm headed towards a Sears, a store like Walmart. I'm headed towards and I turn it. I was about to hit these two metal brick beams and I just drive home and park the car and just go to bed. I wake up at like 7:00, my mama whipping me with a station wagon like 7:00 in the morning. Telling me I totaled the car. I drove the car home. I was so gone. I drove the car off and just parked it. The whole side of the car totaled. No tires, no nothing. I just went home. That's how gone I was. But I've been through that experience and stopping, like the withdrawal from it. That shit damn near killed me. The withdrawal from it. Trying to get off it.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: losing teammate Lorenzo Taliaferro to addiction after shared struggles
quotes.quote: I still remember when I got that call. It was the night before we played a Thursday night game against the Chargers. I was on a hot streak. I had like 200 a week before, a couple weeks before. I'm just like in the peak of my career and I get this call from the dude who was his chef, who we called Chef. I still don't even know his real name, but he was like, 'I just want to let you know that Zoe died.' And I was like, 'I think I know what it was from.' That shit just fried me because I didn't, I wasn't like, I was in the building, I was talking to dudes, laughing, joking, all that shit. But when we left the building, I wasn't letting nobody see what I was doing. He was the only dude I was kicking it with. We were just playing 2K, going to the store, getting food, just chilling for real. It got to a point where we were both like, 'Man, we got to stop this shit. We got to get our shit together,' and it would keep going because the hooks are in us. It's just crazy to see, to get that phone call and see the fork in the road and how far where he's at and where I was at. It was just like, 'Damn, I wish he could have came this route too.' That's the nature of the beast. Rest in peace.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: taking a job stocking shelves at Sprouts after rehab for structure
quotes.quote: I was just really looking for structure coming out of rehab. If I don't have structure, I'm going to be back on bullshit. This dude, my dad, who he played pickup with, he was one of the store managers at Sprouts. He was like, 'Yeah, we can get him a job. He can come in whenever.' So I'm in there. People recognizing you? Not really, because at that time, I'd been in the league, but I've been recognized. There was one moment, there was this chick that was a couple years older than me on the volleyball team at Georgia Tech back when I was at school and I was always trying to get at but couldn't. She saw me in there working at Sprouts. I'm like, 'Damn.' But nobody really noticed me. I wasn't really a big name at that time. People were just like, 'Why the fuck you in here? You should be on the field somewhere.' I'm like, 'It's a long story. There's a lot going on with that.'

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: career turnaround under Jon Gruden with the Oakland Raiders
quotes.quote: That was just how that even happened was wild. It would be me, RG3 and Jordan Lazzley, he played at UCLA. He's a wide receiver. We would go out before the games and get extra routes in because we weren't suiting up. That week we had played the Raiders and every week we'd gone out there. But that week I was just like, 'Man, I'm tired of this shit. I've been putting all this work. Ain't nothing going to happen. I'm not going to play any game again.' I was thinking about not going out there and running routes for the warmups. If I didn't, they wouldn't have seen me working out because they saw me running and they were like, 'Fuck, they were bad. We're just going to sign him and see what we can work with.' Went there the next week, played the last six games, started the next season. They just gave me the keys because Jared Cook was a Pro Bowler in 2018 at tight end. They just let him walk and gave me opportunity. It was just up from there. He was scheming me up all which type of ways, putting me in every position. If you want to get open, if you really want to eat, you got to line up in all these different positions. They would show me Julio Jones, like he lined up in every single position. I was like, 'All right, I'm going to learn all this shit.' That kind of opened the doors.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: mental state after career turnaround and Jon Gruden's impact
quotes.quote: That shit was a high, bro. It was really like, I look back now and it's like, 'Damn, it almost happened so fast.' From working at Sprouts to signing the first contract I signed that was the highest deal for a tight end at the time. That was less than two years, like 18 months. Working at a grocery store, stocking shelves, going and getting backstock to being one of the best players in my position. I was definitely still sober and everything, but I felt there was more work that I needed to dive deeper on within myself. The success and where life was going, it was like, 'Everything good, let's just roll, let's just live.' It was such a huge blessing in some ways, and in some ways it kind of took me off course a little bit with work I needed to just dive deeper on. I think Gruden was hilarious. He loved putting dudes in positions to turn their careers around. He would give you opportunities, bro. I wouldn't have a career, I probably wouldn't be here today without him giving me an opportunity to show what I got.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: impact of athletes sharing their struggles and showing humanity
quotes.quote: A lot of times, like the shit that we can do, we're so like, it feels like there's such a big gap between us. But we're normal people. You show that humanity side. I realized that too because I mean, I think when I that Hard Knocks training camp, I had maybe like 2,000 followers on Instagram. I went and shared, like the first time I had shared my story, I checked my Instagram, I had 30,000. I was like, 'Something got to be wrong.' But everybody was like, 'Thank you for sharing that. My son's going through this, my cousin's going through this, my brother's going through this.' It's just like, 'Oh, this is purpose for me.' That's what inspired me to take steps even further of trying to just be vulnerable with what I got going.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: stepping away from the NFL to address mental health and emptiness
quotes.quote: I was still feeling like I had done a lot of work on myself to get to this position. I feel like almost like the same level of pain and emptiness as far as where I feel like my life is heading. It's not even the drugs and alcohol aren't even the picture, so I can't even blame that. So it's like, 'What is something got to change?' That's the work I was telling you about, like when shit got successful so fast, there was so much more I needed to explore from just like that pain I was carrying from really young. I just didn't feel like my life was heading in the direction I wanted it to, and I felt like I needed to explore that more. I didn't feel like I really could give all I could to it while still playing. Even though it was at the time where I'm still at the peak of my ability and stuff like that. I realized how crazy of a decision that is, how drastic a decision walking away from that level of money and stuff like that.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: healing process after stepping away from football and divorce
quotes.quote: It was just like dealing with, I want to say, grief for the first time in my life. I'd never lost nobody close to me or family members or nothing like that. Grieving because that's the same time I had got divorced and stepping away from football, which is like, I've been playing football since I was four, so it's a part of my whole journey. All those pieces are kind of getting pulled back and sitting with all the emotions that come up with those things. That's where I feel like diving into music, that shit went to another level for me because that was a real way for me to express myself through that time. Doing a lot of therapy, doing a lot of trauma work, inner child work, deep stuff that allowed me to have a more balanced view towards football because it was always just so up and down. I hate this shit, I love this shit. I could live with both. Approach it from that balanced place and that opportunity to go to the Dolphins presented itself. I'm like, 'I'm ready to go. I feel like this is presented by the universe in a way I can't deny.'

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: the 'natural drug' of playing football after returning from hiatus
quotes.quote: That shit was wild. I still can't put that into words because that's the first game I played in in two years. Two touchdowns. I got to training camp, the second week we're doing a speed workout. I ain't sprinted in two years, I wasn't doing the workouts. Damn near tore my hip flexor from my quad. It was like a grade three. That shit had me out the entire training camp. I need training camp to get my skills back because I ain't played in two years. No training camp. Out the first three games. I have like two limited practices before that Jets game that I played. So I'm going into it like, 'I really ain't done nothing.' We're just going to go out here and just wing it. See what happens. It was like third down, red zone, be ready. Get into the game. I'm like, 'I don't know how this shit about to go.' First play, we got one yard. Second play, I think we got two yards. It's third and seven. I'm like, 'Up, it's third down.' They tell me go in the game. You know off the play that they call where you're at in the progression. They call play. I'm the number one option. I'm like, 'If it's man, I'm getting the ball.' I line up, I go in motion, it's man. It's just like, 'Go to the middle, catch my first down.' I was like, 'Oh, we back.' That's like a natural drug. That's like high off life. It felt like somebody interviewed me and said like, 'I felt like I was on drugs.' They were like, 'What the fuck is he talking about?' But I'm like, that shit, the rush of that shit. I feel like my nervous system, I'm used to chilling in my backyard, smoking a cigar, hanging out with my friends, going on a walk on a trail. My nervous system ain't been back in that action pack. 80,000 people screaming for you. Fourth down in the red zone, got to have it up top in the back of the end zone. That shit was just like the craziest buzz I had ever felt playing football.

quotes.speaker: Darren Waller
quotes.summary_phrase: Darren Waller celebrates nine years of sobriety after addiction
quotes.quote: August will be nine years. Congratulations, bro. Congratulations on, man, all you, all the things you've overcome. Thank you for being open and vulnerable and sharing your journey with us. We're going to continue to root for you and hope and pray that you land somewhere that you want to this next season. We get to cheer for you a little bit more. Appreciate you all, man. That's a wrap.
